newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow backs Zil carmaker loan, eyes Moskvich.
newsitem.headline: Moscow backs Zil carmaker loan, eyes Moskvich.

text.p: The Moscow city government on Tuesday guaranteed a 200 billion rouble ($36 million) loan to Russian truck and limousine-maker AMO ZiL and set its sights on a controlling interest in Moscow car-maker Moskvich.
A city hall spokesman said mayor Yury Luzhkov had signed the order guaranteeing the loan to Moscow-based ZiL, to be used for operating capital.
The loan may be extended to up to one year but requires monthly payments to a consortium of Russian banks which may charge up to 48 percent annualised interest.
Moscow already controls at least 30 percent of the shares of ZiL, and Luzhkov has often lauded a new medium-light truck which he hopes will compete with AO Gaz's popular 1.5 tonne GAZelle truck.
ZiL turned out 18,000 vehicles in 1995, and the State Statistics Committee said its October output was up 200 percent on September.

Interfax news agency quoted Viktor Teleshov, Moscow's first deputy minister of science and industrial policy, as saying the city also planned to acquire 60 percent of car-maker Moskvich, which stopped its assembly lines early this year.

As the largest creditor of the company, which is currently undergoing bankruptcy proceedings which will determine how it will reorganise, Moscow would expect to head the board of directors, it quoted Teleshov as saying.

Moskvich is negotiating with car-maker Renault to build French autos in Moscow, and Renault said recently a contract for selling 40,000 motors per year to Moskvich was close to receiving commercial bank backing.
There has been no information of other new credits.
A Federal Bankruptcy Administration official said last week that it was overseeing Moskvich, which hired a new chief executive officer on November 29.

Interfax said Moskvich owed the federal government 200 billion roubles out of a total three trillion roubles of debt and quoted Teleshov as saying it would take 177 billion roubles to resume production.
